title: Gevini
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [the beginning of Shekalim, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.5.1.14): he was appointed in the Temple to proclaim, “Priests, rise for the service; Levites, to your platform; Israelites, to your stations.” King Agrippas heard his voice eight parasangs away. Hyman cites [Mishnah Tamid 3:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Tamid.3.8) for the report that Gevini the herald was heard in Jericho, ten parasangs from Jerusalem. [Yoma 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.20b.7-9) says that Agrippas heard his voice three parasangs away (see [Tosafot Yeshanim there](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_Yeshanim_on_Yoma.20b.4)) and gave him many gifts.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: The linked Shekalim gives eight parasangs and gifts. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=829&lang=en) points to the beginning of that chapter.

Tamid says Gevini was heard in Jericho. [Hyman’s printed p. 300](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=331) cites 3:8, with מ״ח where the supplied Hebrew has מ״מ.

Yoma gives Agrippas three parasangs and states the ten-parasang distance in a separate comparison with the High Priest. Tosafot Yeshanim discusses ways of reconciling the sources and records the view that they disagree.
